knowledge-base.overview: Spring Boot 3.x / Kotlin 1.9+ guardrails, patterns, and best practices for enterprise REST APIs and microservices using idiomatic Kotlin. Covers Kotlin data classes as entities and DTOs, constructor injection, @field: annotation targets for validation, null safety in repositories, Kotlin coroutines with Spring WebFlux, @Transactional usage, GlobalExceptionHandler, Spring Security (stateless), and Gradle Kotlin DSL. Loaded automatically when agents work on Spring Boot Kotlin projects.

core-principles.principle: Use Kotlin idioms throughout: data classes for entities/DTOs, constructor injection (default), null safety, extension functions.
Controller -> Service -> Repository. Controllers return ResponseEntity with explicit status. Services contain transactions and business logic. Repositories are Spring Data interfaces.
Repository findBy methods return T? for nullable finds. Use ?. and ?: consistently. Avoid !! without prior null checks.
Use data classes for JPA entities (plugin.jpa auto-generates no-arg constructors), DTOs, and config. Use copy() for updates.
Constructor injection is Kotlin's default. Never use @Autowired or lateinit var for dependencies.

guardrail.rule: Never use lateinit var for dependencies. Constructor injection is idiomatic and enforced.
Never expose JPA entities in controller responses. Always return DTOs from the service layer.
Use @field: annotation target prefix for validation annotations on data class properties.
Never use ddl-auto=update in production. Use Flyway or Liquibase migrations.
Use @Transactional for write operations, @Transactional(readOnly = true) for reads.
Use @Valid @RequestBody on all incoming request bodies in controllers.
Never use !! operator without a prior null check or explicit invariant justification.
Never mix reactive and blocking code in the same call chain.
Use Spring profiles (application-{profile}.yml) for all environment-specific configuration. Never hardcode secrets.
Use @ConfigurationProperties data classes for type-safe configuration. Annotate the main class or a @Configuration class with @EnableConfigurationProperties.
Use the open modifier (or plugin.spring) on @Component, @Service, @Controller classes. Kotlin classes are final by default; Spring needs to proxy them.
